label: adhesin
assay_summary: Hyphae of a targeted SC3 disruptant and of the thn regulatory mutant attach much less firmly to Teflon than wild type, SC3 protein is found between the wall and the Teflon, and purified SC3 monomers self-assemble onto hydrophobic solids into an SDS- and 100 C-resistant 10 nm film; a 2026 quantitative bonding study confirms weaker attachment of the sc3 deletion strain to Teflon.
notes: Class I hydrophobin, mature protein 100-101 aa after signal cleavage, 16-22 O-linked mannoses. Adhesion is to abiotic hydrophobic surfaces (Teflon), not to a host. Same protein family as the SC4 hard negative in this table, so the pair is a deliberate within-family positive/negative contrast.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: Deleting SC15 alone leaves attachment to hydrophobic surfaces unchanged, but a delta-SC3 delta-SC15 double mutant almost completely loses attachment (and aerial hyphae), so SC15 mediates attachment when SC3 is absent; a later quantitative study scored adhesion of the double deletion strain to Teflon, glass and wood.
notes: Secreted 191 aa protein, hydrophilic N-terminal half and strongly hydrophobic C-terminal half, NOT a hydrophobin (lacks the eight conserved Cys). Evidence is conditional on the delta-SC3 background; delta-SC15 alone has no phenotype. Accession is the H4-8 reference-genome protein (191 aa, same length as the protein characterised in strain 4-40); no UniProt entry exists for S. commune SC15, verified via NCBI eutils esummary.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: class I hydrophobin, aerial hyphae formation
assay_summary: A delta-hum2 cross forms fewer aerial hyphae, but colony surface hydrophobicity is unaffected and attachment of hyphae to hydrophobic Teflon is unchanged; the repellent Rep1, not the hydrophobins, is what mediates attachment in U. maydis.
notes: Best class of hard negative: a secreted, Cys-rich, surface-active wall protein in which adhesion was explicitly assayed and found unaffected. Rep1 (Q99109) from the same organism is already in the positive set.

protein_name: Class I hydrophobin hum3 (17 Rep1-like repeats plus a hydrophobin domain)
label: hard_negative
mechanism: repeat-containing class I hydrophobin, KEX2-processed secreted protein
assay_summary: Deleting hum3 on top of hum2 does not further change aerial hyphae formation, surface hydrophobicity or attachment of hyphae to hydrophobic Teflon; Hum3 is cleaved at KEX2 sites during passage through the secretory pathway, and single hydrophobin or repellent-like knockouts do not affect pathogenicity.
notes: Valuable negative for repeat-based adhesin prediction: 828 aa with 17 tandem Rep1-like repeats separated by KEX2 sites, i.e. the same architecture as the Rep1 positive, yet attachment was tested and unaffected. UniProt gene field reads him3 (typo for hum3) with locus UMAG_04433.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Gas channels in delta-SC4 fruiting bodies fill with water, unlike wild type, showing that SC4 lines the channels with a hydrophobic membrane for gas exchange; SC4 expressed from the SC3 promoter in a delta-SC3 monokaryon cannot fully substitute for SC3, and the dikaryon-specific SC1 and SC6 hydrophobins do not substitute for SC4.
notes: Judgement call: the demonstrated function is non-adhesive (channel lining), but attachment of a delta-SC4 single mutant to a hydrophobic surface is not reported in the primary paper, so this is function_shown rather than adhesion-tested-and-unaffected. Deliberate within-family contrast with the SC3 positive.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Point mutations in the Cda1 active site leave protein stability and cell-wall localisation intact but reduce chitosan production and attenuate virulence in CBA/J mice, and cda1 deletion strains make correspondingly less chitosan, showing Cda1 acts catalytically as a wall-remodelling enzyme.
notes: GPI-anchored, Ser/Thr-rich, heavily glycosylated wall protein, i.e. exactly the feature profile a composition-based adhesin predictor calls positive. No adhesion assay has been published for cda1 mutants. Family conflict to note: the paralogue Cda3/MP84 (P82476) is already in the positive set on the strength of an epithelial-adhesion inhibition assay.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: A cda1 cda2 double deletion makes no detectable chitosan and is completely cleared in CBA/J, C57BL/6 and BALB/c mice, while cda2 cda3 retains wild-type virulence, showing that Cda2 acts with Cda1 as a chitin deacetylase.
notes: This is the protein often cited as the adhesin Mp98: that literature shows T-cell stimulation and mannosylation, never an adhesion assay, so it fails the inclusion rule and is placed here on its demonstrated enzymatic function instead. Same family conflict as CDA1 with respect to Cda3/MP84.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: extracellular mannoprotein haemophore, iron acquisition from heme
assay_summary: Recombinant Cig1 titrated with heme shows the absorbance spectrum of a heme-binding protein, cig1 deletion delays growth on heme at physiological pH and changes susceptibility to non-iron metalloporphyrins, so this surface mannoprotein functions as a hemophore.
notes: Abundant, iron-regulated, secreted/surface mannoprotein; another high-glycosylation surface protein with a demonstrated non-adhesion function. Gene identity taken from the UniProt annotation (cytokine-inducing glycoprotein, locus CNAG_01653 in H99) matching the CIG1 gene studied in the primary paper; no adhesion assay published.

protein_name: Secreted effector Pit2 (protein important for tumors 2)
label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Pit2 inhibits a set of apoplastic maize cysteine proteases, a synthetic peptide of its conserved motif reproduces full inhibitory activity, and a Pit2 variant mutated in that motif fails to restore virulence of the pit2 deletion mutant, showing the protein acts as a protease inhibitor.
notes: Small secreted biotrophic-interface effector with a demonstrated biochemical non-adhesion function. Apoplastic rather than covalently wall-bound; included as a surface/interface protein negative. Adhesion was not assayed for pit2 mutants.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Plb1 is a GPI-anchored wall enzyme carrying three demonstrated activities (PLB, LPL, LPTA), and although a plb1 deletion in H99 adheres about 69 percent less to A549 lung epithelial cells and specific anti-PLB1 antibodies and PLB-selective (but not LPL- or LPTA-selective) inhibitors cut adhesion of wild type by 33-58 percent, the adhesion loss is indirect: 0.1-2 mM exogenous palmitic acid restores adhesion of the live plb1 mutant dose-dependently (to 67 percent), showing the released fatty acid, not the protein, is what sticks.
notes: adhesion phenotype on deletion but indirect mechanism; owner decision 2026-11-26 to label hard_negative. GPI-anchored, beta-1,6-glucan-linked wall protein with no adhesive domain - a deliberate trap row for predictors that score GPI plus Ser/Thr-rich surface proteins as adhesins. Locus CNAG_06085, H99 (serotype A), the same background used in the adhesion assay.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Cps1 is a membrane glycosyltransferase whose synthase function was shown directly by heterologous expression (CPS1 expressed in S. cerevisiae and E. coli makes hyaluronic acid) and by hyaluronan ELISA plus site-directed mutagenesis of its conserved glycosyltransferase domains, and although a cps1 deletion in a serotype D strain significantly reduces association with human brain microvascular endothelial cells, the adhesion loss is indirect: the actual CD44 ligand is the hyaluronic acid polymer the enzyme makes, and hyaluronidase or 4-methylumbelliferone treatment of wild-type cells reduces HBMEC binding in proportion to hyaluronic acid content.
notes: adhesion phenotype on deletion but indirect mechanism; owner decision 2026-11-26 to label hard_negative. Strain note: Q6YNJ4 is the cloned CPS1 gene product (EMBL AY063511, 449 aa) and the deletion was made in a serotype D (JEC21-lineage) strain; the H99 (serotype A) orthologue is J9VUH0 / CNAG_04320, 451 aa, if a single-strain reference proteome is needed. Integral membrane glycosyltransferase, not a wall-surface protein, so it is also a negative for the surface-localisation feature.
